The screenshot displays a **Next.js development environment** (specifically version 16.1.3, marked as "stale" with Turbopack) showing a **build error** in a web application. The interface is structured as a single-page error report with a clean, minimalistic design typical of developer tools.


### **Overall Layout & Structure**
The page has a **white background** with a centered, bordered container (light gray border) holding the error details. The top of the page includes a navigation bar with a "1/1" indicator (suggesting a single page in the build) and a Next.js/Turbopack status badge. The main content is divided into a header (with the error title) and a code block (with line numbers, syntax highlighting, and error details).


### **Top Navigation Bar**
- **Left Side**: A back/forward navigation control showing "1/1" (likely indicating the current page in a multi-page build, though only one page exists here).  
- **Right Side**: A badge with an orange circle and text: "Next.js 16.1.3 (stale) Turbopack" (indicating the framework version and build tool). Next to the badge are three icons: a circular refresh button, a square (possibly for view mode), and a user/profile icon.


### **Error Header**
- **Title**: "Build Error" in **red text** (bold, larger font) to draw attention.  
- **Subtitle**: "Export POSTerminal doesn't exist in target module" in **black text** (smaller font, bold) below the title.


### **Code Block Section**
A bordered (light gray) code editor area containing the error details:  
- **File Path**: A gray icon (resembling a gear or settings) followed by the file path: `./src/app/page.tsx (25:1)` (indicating the error is in `page.tsx` at line 25, column 1). A copy icon (clipboard) is on the right of the file path.  
- **Code Snippet**: A multi-line code block with **line numbers** (23–28) in gray, left-aligned. The code uses **syntax highlighting**:  
  - **Red text**: The problematic line: `import { POSTerminal } from '@components/grocery/pos-terminal';` (line 25).  
  - **Blue text**: Other import statements (e.g., `import { GroceryStore } from '@components/grocery/grocery-store';` on line 23).  
  - **Black text**: Remaining code (e.g., `import { businesses } from '@components/grocery/data';` on line 26).  
- **Error Message**: Below the code, a detailed error explanation in black text:  
  > "The export POSTerminal was not found in module [project/src/components/grocery/pos-terminal.tsx (app-client)] (ecmascript). Did you mean to import the module 'POSTerminal'? All exports of the module are statically known (It doesn't have dynamic exports). So it's known statically that the requested export..." (text is truncated).  
- **Import Traces**: Two subsections labeled "Import traces:" with bullet points:  
  - **Client Component Browser**: `./src/app/page.tsx [Client Component Browser]`  
  - **Client Component SSR**: `./src/app/page.tsx [Client Component SSR]`  
  Each bullet includes the file path and component type in gray text.


### **Colors & UI Elements**
- **Primary Background**: White.  
- **Borders**: Light gray (around the code block and navigation bar).  
- **Text Colors**:  
  - Error title: Red (bold).  
  - Subtitle: Black (bold).  
  - Code: Line numbers (gray), syntax-highlighted code (red for errors, blue for imports, black for other text).  
  - Error message: Black.  
- **Icons**: Gray (file path icon, copy icon, navigation icons).  
- **Badge**: Orange circle with black text.  


### **Key Takeaways**
The screenshot captures a **Next.js build error** caused by a missing export (`POSTerminal`) in a grocery-related component. The interface is designed for developers, with clear visual hierarchy (error title in red, code with syntax highlighting, and detailed traces) to help diagnose the issue. The layout is minimal, focusing on presenting the error and its context without unnecessary distractions.
